doc:
`nth_rw` is a variant of `rw` that only changes the `n₁, ..., nₖ`ᵗʰ _occurrence_ of the expression
to be rewritten. Like `rw`, and unlike `nth_rewrite`, it will try to close the goal by trying `rfl`
afterwards. `nth_rw n₁ ... nₖ [eq₁, eq₂,..., eqₘ]` will rewrite the `n₁, ..., nₖ`ᵗʰ _occurrence_ of
each of the `m` equalities `eqᵢ`in that order. Occurrences are counted beginning with `1` in
order of precedence. For example,
```lean
example (h : a = 1) : a + a + a + a + a = 5 := by
  nth_rw 2 3 [h]
/-
a: ℕ
h: a = 1
⊢ a + 1 + 1 + a + a = 5
-/
```
Notice that the second and third occurrences of `a` from the left have been rewritten by
`nth_rw`.

To understand the importance of order of precedence, consider the example below
```lean
example (a b c : Nat) : (a + b) + c = (b + a) + c := by
  nth_rewrite 2 [Nat.add_comm] -- ⊢ (b + a) + c = (b + a) + c
```
Here, although the occurrence parameter is `2`, `(a + b)` is rewritten to `(b + a)`. This happens
because in order of precedence, the first occurrence of `_ + _` is the one that adds `a + b` to `c`.
The occurrence in `a + b` counts as the second occurrence.

If a term `t` is introduced by rewriting with `eqᵢ`, then this instance of `t` will be counted as an
_occurrence_ of `t` for all subsequent rewrites of `t` with `eqⱼ` for `j > i`. This behaviour is
illustrated by the example below
```lean
example (h : a = a + b) : a + a + a + a + a = 0 := by
  nth_rw 3 [h, h]
/-
a b: ℕ
h: a = a + b
⊢ a + a + (a + b + b) + a + a = 0
-/
```
Here, the first `nth_rw` with `h` introduces an additional occurrence of `a` in the goal. That is,
the goal state after the first rewrite looks like below
```lean
/-
a b: ℕ
h: a = a + b
⊢ a + a + (a + b) + a + a = 0
-/
```
This new instance of `a` also turns out to be the third _occurrence_ of `a`.  Therefore,
the next `nth_rw` with `h` rewrites this `a`.

Further, `nth_rw` will close the remaining goal with `rfl` if possible.

  let __do_lift ← Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.Result.insertInArray.findDuplicate✝ isDup res arr
  match __do_lift with
    | some idx =>

        pure
          (Array.binInsert (fun x1 x2 => decide (x1 < x2))
            (arr.modify idx fun x =>
              { filtered := none, unfiltered := x.unfiltered, key := x.key, pattern := x.pattern })
            res)
      else
        pure
          (Array.binInsert (fun x1 x2 => decide (x1 < x2)) arr
            { filtered := none, unfiltered := res.unfiltered, key := res.key,
              pattern := res.pattern })
    | x => pure (Array.binInsert (fun x1 x2 => decide (x1 < x2)) arr res)

doc:
This function is passed to `MVarId.gcongr` as the main discharger.
It doesn't try to prove the goal, but instead observes what the goal is,
to help determine which lemmas could work with `grw`.

If the selected grewrite position is valid, then `ref` is set, and a dummy error is thrown.
Note that this function will be called at most once,
so we don't lose information by throwing an error.

fun ref hyp? fvar goal => do
  let __do_lift ← goal.getType
  let e ← Lean.instantiateMVars __do_lift

    | (relation.app lhs).app rhs =>
      match relation.getAppFn with
      | Lean.Expr.const relName us =>
        have __do_jp := fun __r =>
          have __do_jp := fun symm => do
            let __do_lift ← Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.gcongrBackward✝ relName relation symm
            ST.Ref.set ref __do_lift
            throw
                (Lean.Exception.error default
                  ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format) "dummyError"));
          if (lhs.cleanupAnnotations == fvar) = true then do
            let symm ← pure hyp?
            __do_jp symm
          else
            if (rhs.cleanupAnnotations == fvar) = true then do
              let symm ← pure !hyp?
              __do_jp symm
            else do
              let symm ←
                Lean.throwError
                    (Lean.toMessageData e ++ Lean.toMessageData " doesn't have " ++
                        Lean.toMessageData fvar ++
                      Lean.toMessageData " on either side")
              __do_jp symm;
        if
            (match relName with
              | `Eq => true
              | `Iff => true
              | x => false) =
              true then
          do
          let __r ←
            Lean.throwError
                (Lean.toMessageData e ++ Lean.toMessageData " is not a generalized relation")
          __do_jp __r
        else __do_jp ()
      | x => Lean.throwError (Lean.toMessageData e ++ Lean.toMessageData " is not a relation")
    | x =>
      Lean.throwError
        (Lean.toMessageData "`" ++ Lean.toMessageData e ++ Lean.toMessageData "` is not a relation")

  (errorRef : Lean.Meta.FoldDeclErrorRef) (env : Lean.Environment) (init : α)
  (act : α → Lean.Name → Lean.ConstantInfo → Lean.MetaM α) (mctx : Lean.Meta.Context)

fun {α} ngen errorRef env init act mctx cctx start stop => do
  let __do_lift ← liftM IO.getNumHeartbeats
  have cctx : Lean.Core.Context :=
    { fileName := cctx.fileName, fileMap := cctx.fileMap, options := cctx.options,
      currRecDepth := cctx.currRecDepth, maxRecDepth := cctx.maxRecDepth, ref := cctx.ref,
      currNamespace := cctx.currNamespace, openDecls := cctx.openDecls, initHeartbeats := __do_lift,
      maxHeartbeats := cctx.maxHeartbeats, quotContext := cctx.quotContext,
      currMacroScope := cctx.currMacroScope, diag := cctx.diag, cancelTk? := cctx.cancelTk?,
      suppressElabErrors := cctx.suppressElabErrors,
      inheritedTraceOptions := cctx.inheritedTraceOptions }
  have go : Lean.MetaM α :=
    have a := init;
    do
    let __s ←
      forIn (start...stop) a fun i __s =>
          have a := __s;
          do
          liftM Lean.Core.checkInterrupted
          have modName : Lean.Name := env.header.moduleNames[i]!
          match env.header.moduleData[i]! with
            |
            { isModule := isModule, imports := imports, constNames := constNames,
                constants := constants, extraConstNames := extraConstNames, entries := entries } =>
              do
              let __s ←
                forIn' (*...constNames.size) a fun i h __s =>
                    have a := __s;
                    have name := constNames[i];
                    have constInfo := constants[i]!;
                    do
                    let a ← Lean.Meta.visitConst✝ modName errorRef act a name constInfo
                    pure (ForInStep.yield a)
              have a : α := __s
              pure (ForInStep.yield a)
    have a : α := __s
    pure a
  (go.run' mctx).run' cctx { env := env, ngen := ngen }

doc:
Fold through all imported constants using `act`.
This uses parallelism, with each thread independently folding over a subset of modules.
The array of tasks is returned, so this function typically returns before all tasks have finished.
The results can then be combined using `Array.foldl`.

value.text:
fun {α} init cfg act constantsPerTask => do
  let env ← Lean.getEnv
  let numModules : ℕ := env.header.moduleData.size
  have mctx : Lean.Meta.Context := { keyedConfig := cfg.toConfigWithKey }
  let cctx ← read
  let errorRef ← liftM (IO.mkRef ∅)
  have tasks : Array (Task (Except Lean.Exception α)) := #[]
  have start : ℕ := 0
  have count : ℕ := 0
  let __s ←
    forIn' (*...numModules) (tasks, start, count) fun idx h __s =>
        have tasks := __s.1;
        have __s := __s.2;
        have start := __s.1;
        have count := __s.2;
        have count := count + env.header.moduleData[idx].constants.size;
        if count > constantsPerTask then do
          let __do_lift ← Lean.getNGen
          match __do_lift.mkChild with
            | (childNGen, parentNGen) => do
              Lean.setNGen parentNGen
              let t ←
                liftM
                    (Lean.Meta.foldModules✝ childNGen errorRef env init act mctx cctx start
                        (idx + 1)).asTask
              have tasks : Array (Task (Except Lean.Exception α)) := tasks.push t
              have count : ℕ := 0
              have start : ℕ := idx + 1
              pure (ForInStep.yield (tasks, start, count))
        else pure (ForInStep.yield (tasks, start, count))
  have tasks : Array (Task (Except Lean.Exception α)) := __s.1
  have __s : ℕ × ℕ := __s.2
  have start : ℕ := __s.1
  have __do_jp :
    Unit →
      Array (Task (Except Lean.Exception α)) →
        Lean.CoreM (Array (Task (Except Lean.Exception α)) × Lean.Meta.FoldDeclErrorRef) :=
    fun __r tasks => pure (tasks, errorRef)
  if start < numModules then do
      let __do_lift ← Lean.getNGen
      match __do_lift.mkChild with
        | (childNGen, parentNGen) => do
          Lean.setNGen parentNGen
          let t ←
            liftM
                (Lean.Meta.foldModules✝ childNGen errorRef env init act mctx cctx start
                    numModules).asTask
          have tasks : Array (Task (Except Lean.Exception α)) := tasks.push t
          __do_jp () tasks
    else __do_jp () tasks

fun {α} modName errorRef act a name constInfo => do
  let e ←
    tryCatch
        (do
          let r ← act a name constInfo
          ExceptT.run (pure r))
        fun e =>
        have msg :=
          Lean.toMessageData "Processing failure with " ++ Lean.toMessageData name ++
                  Lean.toMessageData " in " ++
                Lean.toMessageData modName ++
              Lean.toMessageData ":\n  " ++
            Lean.toMessageData e.toMessageData;
        do
        ST.Ref.modify errorRef fun x => msg :: x
        EarlyReturnT.return a
  EarlyReturn.runK e (fun r => pure r) fun r => pure r

doc:
Format a `RefinedDiscrTree` as a flowchart.
- Non-terminal nodes are of the form `{key} =>`, followed by all of the following nodes,
  indented with 2 more spaces.
- Terminal nodes have either "entries", containing the return values,
  or "pending entries", for nodes that have not been evaluated/expanded.

For example:
```
Discrimination tree flowchart:
⟨HMul.hMul, 6⟩ =>
  ⟨Int, 0⟩ =>
    ⟨Int, 0⟩ =>
      * =>
        * =>
          *0 =>
            *0 =>
              pending entries: #[mul_self]
            *1 =>
              entries: #[mul_comm]
            ⟨Neg.neg, 3⟩ =>
              ⟨Int, 0⟩ =>
                * =>
                  *1 =>
                    entries: #[mul_neg]
            1 =>
              pending entries: #[mul_one]
          ⟨Neg.neg, 3⟩ =>
            pending entries: #[neg_mul]
          1 =>
            *0 =>
              entries: #[one_mul]
```

value.text:
fun {α} [Std.ToFormat α] tree =>
  have lines :=
    Std.HashMap.fold
      (fun lines key trie =>
        lines.push
          (Std.Format.nest 2
            (Std.format key ++ Std.format " =>" ++ Std.format Std.Format.line ++
              Std.format (Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.format.go tree trie))))
      #[] tree.root;
  if lines.size = 0 then Std.format "<empty discrimination tree>"
  else
    Std.Format.text "Discrimination tree flowchart:\n" ++
      Std.Format.joinSep lines.toList (Std.Format.text "\n")

doc:
The stack, used to emulate recursion. It contains the list of all expressions for which the
keys still need to be computed, in that order.

doc:
Compute the hash of a `RefinedDiscrTree.Key`.

Note: at the root, `.const` is the most common key, and it is very uncommon
to get the same constant name with a different arity.
So for performance, we just use `hash name` to hash `.const name _`.

value.text:
fun x =>
  match x with
  | Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Key.star => 0
  | Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Key.labelledStar id => mixHash 5 (hash id)
  | Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Key.opaque => 1
  | Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Key.const name nargs => hash name
  | Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Key.fvar fvarId nargs =>
    mixHash 6 (mixHash (hash fvarId) (hash nargs))
  | Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Key.bvar idx nargs => mixHash 7 (mixHash (hash idx) (hash nargs))
  | Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Key.lit v => mixHash 8 (hash v)
  | Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Key.sort => 2
  | Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Key.lam => 3
  | Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Key.forall => 4
  | Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Key.proj name idx nargs =>
    mixHash (hash nargs) (mixHash (hash name) (hash idx))

      let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.getConfig
      have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.MetaM (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key × Array Lean.Expr) := fun __r =>
        have nargs := e.getAppNumArgs;
        pure (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key.const c nargs, e.getAppRevArgs)
      if (__do_lift.isDefEqStuckEx && e.hasExprMVar) = true then do
          let __do_lift ← Lean.isReducible c
          if __do_lift = true then do
              let __r ← Lean.Meta.throwIsDefEqStuck
              __do_jp __r
            else do
              let __do_lift ← Lean.getEnv
              match Lean.Meta.isMatcherAppCore? __do_lift e with
                | some matcherInfo =>
                  have args := e.getAppArgs;
                  have start := matcherInfo.getFirstDiscrPos;
                  do
                  forIn (Std.Rco.Sliceable.mkSlice args start...start + matcherInfo.numDiscrs)
                      PUnit.unit fun arg __s =>
                      if arg.hasExprMVar = true then do
                        Lean.Meta.throwIsDefEqStuck
                        pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
                      else pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
                  __do_jp ()
                | x => do
                  let __do_lift ← Lean.isRec c
                  if __do_lift = true then do
                      let __r ← Lean.Meta.throwIsDefEqStuck
                      __do_jp __r
                    else __do_jp ()
        else __do_jp ()
    | Lean.Expr.fvar fvarId =>
      have nargs := e.getAppNumArgs;
      pure (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key.fvar fvarId nargs, e.getAppRevArgs)
    | Lean.Expr.mvar mvarId =>
      if isMatch = true then pure (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key.other, #[])
      else do
        let cfg ← Lean.Meta.getConfig
        if cfg.isDefEqStuckEx = true then pure (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key.star, #[])
          else do
            let __do_lift ← mvarId.isReadOnlyOrSyntheticOpaque
            if __do_lift = true then pure (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key.other, #[])
              else pure (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key.star, #[])
    | Lean.Expr.proj s i a =>
      have nargs := e.getAppNumArgs;
      pure (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key.proj s i nargs, #[a] ++ e.getAppRevArgs)
    | Lean.Expr.forallE binderName d b binderInfo =>
      have __do_jp := fun b =>
        if b.hasLooseBVars = true then pure (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key.other, #[])
        else pure (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key.arrow, #[d, b]);
      if b.hasLooseBVars = true then do
        let b ← liftM (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.MatchClone.elimLooseBVarsByBeta b)
        __do_jp b
      else do
        let b ← pure b
        __do_jp b
    | Lean.Expr.bvar deBruijnIndex => pure (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key.other, #[])
    | Lean.Expr.letE declName type value body nondep =>
      pure (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key.other, #[])
    | Lean.Expr.lam binderName binderType body binderInfo =>
      pure (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key.other, #[])
    | Lean.Expr.mdata data expr => pure (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key.other, #[])
    | fn.app arg => pure (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key.other, #[])
    | Lean.Expr.sort u => pure (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key.other, #[])
  if root = true then __do_jp ()
    else
      match Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.MatchClone.toNatLit? e with
      | some v => pure (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key.lit v, #[])
      | x => __do_jp ()

  (env : Lean.Environment) (modName : Lean.Name) (d : Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.ImportData)
  (cacheRef : IO.Ref Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Cache) (tree : Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.PreDiscrTree α)

fun {α} cctx env modName d cacheRef tree act name constInfo =>
  if constInfo.isUnsafe = true then pure tree
  else
    if Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.blacklistInsertion env name = true then pure tree
    else do
      let __x ← ST.Ref.get cacheRef
      match __x with
        | { ngen := ngen, core := core_cache, «meta» := meta_cache } =>
          have mstate := { cache := meta_cache };
          do
          ST.Ref.set cacheRef (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Cache.empty ngen)
          have ctx : Lean.Meta.Context :=
            {
              keyedConfig :=
                { transparency := Lean.Meta.TransparencyMode.reducible }.toConfigWithKey }
          have cm : Lean.CoreM (Array (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.InitEntry α) × Lean.Meta.State) :=
            (act name constInfo).run ctx mstate
          have cstate : Lean.Core.State := { env := env, ngen := ngen, cache := core_cache }
          let __do_lift ← (cm.run cctx cstate).toBaseIO
          match __do_lift with
            | Except.ok ((a, ms), cs) => do
              ST.Ref.set cacheRef { ngen := cs.ngen, core := cs.cache, «meta» := ms.cache }
              pure (Array.foldl (fun t e => t.push e.key e.entry) tree a)
            | Except.error e =>
              have i := { module := modName, const := name, exception := e };
              do
              ST.Ref.modify d.errors fun x => x.push i
              pure tree

doc:
Returns true iff the argument should be treated as a "wildcard" by the
discrimination tree.

This includes proofs, instance implicit arguments, implicit arguments,
and terms of the form `noIndexing t`

This is a clone of `Lean.Meta.DiscrTree.ignoreArg` and mainly added to
avoid coupling between `DiscrTree` and `LazyDiscrTree` while both are
potentially subject to independent changes.

signature.text:
def Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.MatchClone.ignoreArg (a : Lean.Expr) (i : ℕ)
  (infos : Array Lean.Meta.ParamInfo) : Lean.MetaM Bool

value.text:
fun a i infos =>
  if h : i < infos.size then
    have info := infos[i];
    if info.isInstance = true then pure true
    else
      if (info.isImplicit || info.isStrictImplicit) = true then do
        let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.isType a
        pure !__do_lift
      else Lean.Meta.isProof a
  else Lean.Meta.isProof a

`findMatches` searches for entries in a lazily initialized discriminator tree.

* `ext` should be an environment extension with an IO.Ref for caching the import lazy

theorem Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.createImportedDiscrTree.go.eq_def✝ {m : Type → Type} {α : Type} [Monad m]
  [MonadLiftT BaseIO m] (cctx : Lean.Core.Context) (env : Lean.Environment)
  (act : Lean.Name → Lean.ConstantInfo → Lean.MetaM (Array (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.InitEntry α)))
  (constantsPerTask n : ℕ) (ngen : Lean.NameGenerator)
  (tasks : Array (Task (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.InitResults α))) (start cnt idx : ℕ) :
  Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.createImportedDiscrTree.go✝ cctx env act constantsPerTask n ngen tasks
      start cnt idx =
    if h : idx < env.header.moduleData.size then
      have mdata := env.header.moduleData[idx];
      have cnt := cnt + mdata.constants.size;
      if cnt > constantsPerTask then
        match ngen.mkChild with
        | (childNGen, ngen) => do
          let t ←
            liftM
                (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.createImportedEnvironmentSeq cctx childNGen env act start
                    (idx + 1)).asTask
          Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.createImportedDiscrTree.go✝ cctx env act constantsPerTask n ngen
              (tasks.push t) (idx + 1) 0 (idx + 1)
      else
        Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.createImportedDiscrTree.go✝ cctx env act constantsPerTask n ngen
          tasks start cnt (idx + 1)
    else
      if start < n then
        match ngen.mkChild with
        | (childNGen, snd) => do
          let t ←
            liftM
                (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.createImportedEnvironmentSeq cctx childNGen env act start
                    n).asTask
          pure (tasks.push t)
      else pure tasks

doc:
`LazyDiscrTree` is a variant of the discriminator tree datatype
`DiscrTree` in Lean core that is designed to be efficiently
initializable with a large number of patterns.  This is useful
in contexts such as searching an entire Lean environment for
expressions that match a pattern.

Lazy discriminator trees achieve good performance by minimizing
the amount of work that is done up front to build the discriminator
tree.  When first adding patterns to the tree, only the root
discriminator key is computed and processing the remaining
terms is deferred until demanded by a match.

def Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.createModuleTreeRef {α : Type}
  (entriesForConst :
    Lean.Name → Lean.ConstantInfo → Lean.MetaM (Array (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.InitEntry α)))
  (droppedKeys : List (List Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key))
  (droppedEntriesRef : Option (IO.Ref (Option (Array α))) := none) :
  Lean.MetaM (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.ModuleDiscrTreeRef α)

value.text:
fun {α} entriesForConst droppedKeys droppedEntriesRef => do
  let __do_lift ← Lean.getOptions
  Lean.profileitM Lean.Exception "build module discriminator tree" __do_lift do
      let t ← liftM (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.createModuleDiscrTree entriesForConst)
      have __do_jp :
        Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree α → Lean.MetaM (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.ModuleDiscrTreeRef α) :=
        fun t => do
        let __do_lift ← liftM (IO.mkRef t)
        pure { ref := __do_lift }
      match droppedEntriesRef with
        | some droppedRef => do
          let __x ← t.extractKeys droppedKeys
          match __x with
            | (extracted, t) => do
              let __do_lift ← ST.Ref.get droppedRef
              have existing : Array α := __do_lift.getD #[]
              ST.Ref.set droppedRef (some (existing ++ extracted))
              let t ← pure t
              __do_jp t
        | x => do
          let t ← t.dropKeys droppedKeys
          __do_jp t

doc:
`findMatchesExt` searches for entries in a lazily initialized discriminator tree.

It provides some additional capabilities beyond `findMatches` to adjust results
based on priority and cache module declarations

* `modulesTreeRef` points to the discriminator tree for local environment.
  Used for caching and created by `createLocalTree`.
* `ext` should be an environment extension with an IO.Ref for caching the import lazy
   discriminator tree.
* `addEntry` is the function for creating discriminator tree entries from constants.
* `droppedKeys` contains keys we do not want to consider when searching for matches.
  It is used for dropping very general keys.
* `constantsPerTask` stores number of constants in imported modules used to
  decide when to create new task.
* `adjustResult` takes the priority and value to produce a final result.
* `ty` is the expression type.

signature.text:
def Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.findMatchesExt {α β : Type}
  (moduleTreeRef : Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.ModuleDiscrTreeRef α)
  (ext : Lean.EnvExtension (IO.Ref (Option (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree α))))
  (addEntry :
    Lean.Name → Lean.ConstantInfo → Lean.MetaM (Array (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.InitEntry α)))
  (droppedKeys : List (List Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key) := []) (constantsPerTask : ℕ := 1000)
  (droppedEntriesRef : Option (IO.Ref (Option (Array α))) := none) (adjustResult : ℕ → α → β)
  (ty : Lean.Expr) : Lean.MetaM (Array β)

value.text:
fun {α β} moduleTreeRef ext addEntry droppedKeys constantsPerTask droppedEntriesRef adjustResult
    ty =>
  do
  let moduleMatches ← Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.findModuleMatches moduleTreeRef ty
  let importMatches ←
    Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.findImportMatches ext addEntry droppedKeys constantsPerTask
        droppedEntriesRef ty
  pure
      (importMatches.appendResultsAux
        (moduleMatches.appendResultsAux (Array.mkEmpty (moduleMatches.size + importMatches.size))
          adjustResult)
        adjustResult)

results with that score. A `score` is the number of non-star matches
in a pattern against the term, and thus bounded by the size of the
term being matched against.  The elements of this array are themselves
arrays of non-empty arrays so that we can defer concatenating results until
needed.

fun {α} ext addEntry droppedKeys constantsPerTask droppedEntriesRef ty => do
  let cctx ← liftM read
  let ngen ← Lean.getNGen
  match ngen.mkChild with
    | (cNGen, ngen) => do
      Lean.setNGen ngen
      let __do_lift ← liftM (IO.mkRef none)
      have x : Inhabited (IO.Ref (Option (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree α))) := { default := __do_lift }
      let __do_lift ← Lean.getEnv
      have ref : IO.Ref (Option (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree α)) := ext.getState __do_lift
      let __do_lift ← ST.Ref.get ref
      let importTree ←
        __do_lift.getDM do
            let __do_lift ← Lean.getOptions
            Lean.profileitM Lean.Exception "lazy discriminator import initialization" __do_lift do
                let __do_lift ← Lean.getEnv
                let t ←
                  Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.createImportedDiscrTree
                      (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.createTreeCtx cctx) cNGen __do_lift addEntry
                      constantsPerTask
                match droppedEntriesRef with
                  | some droppedRef => do
                    let __x ← t.extractKeys droppedKeys
                    match __x with
                      | (extracted, t) => do
                        let __do_lift ← ST.Ref.get droppedRef
                        have existing : Array α := __do_lift.getD #[]
                        ST.Ref.set droppedRef (some (existing ++ extracted))
                        pure t
                  | x => t.dropKeys droppedKeys
      let __x ← importTree.getMatch ty
      match __x with
        | (importCandidates, importTree) => do
          ST.Ref.set ref (some importTree)
          pure importCandidates

fun root todo e =>
  if Lean.Meta.DiscrTree.hasNoindexAnnotation e = true then
    pure (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key.star, todo)
  else do
    let e ← Lean.Meta.DiscrTree.reduceDT e root
    have fn : Lean.Expr := e.getAppFn
    have push :
      Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key →
        ℕ → Array Lean.Expr → Lean.MetaM (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key × Array Lean.Expr) :=
      fun k nargs todo => do
      let info ← Lean.Meta.getFunInfoNArgs fn nargs
      let todo ← Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.MatchClone.pushArgsAux info.paramInfo (nargs - 1) e todo
      pure (k, todo)
    match fn with
      | Lean.Expr.lit v => pure (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key.lit v, todo)
      | Lean.Expr.const c us =>
        have __do_jp := fun __r =>
          have nargs := e.getAppNumArgs;
          push (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key.const c nargs) nargs todo;
        if root = true then __do_jp ()
        else
          match Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.MatchClone.toNatLit? e with
          | some v => pure (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key.lit v, todo)
          | x => do
            let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.MatchClone.shouldAddAsStar c e
            if __do_lift = true then pure (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key.star, todo) else __do_jp ()
      | Lean.Expr.proj s i a => do
        let __do_lift ← Lean.getEnv
        have a : Lean.Expr :=
          if Lean.isClass __do_lift s = true then Lean.Meta.DiscrTree.mkNoindexAnnotation a else a
        have nargs : ℕ := e.getAppNumArgs
        push (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key.proj s i nargs) nargs (todo.push a)
      | Lean.Expr.fvar _fvarId => pure (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key.star, todo)
      | Lean.Expr.mvar mvarId =>
        if (mvarId == Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.MatchClone.tmpMVarId) = true then
          pure (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key.star, todo)
        else failure
      | Lean.Expr.forallE binderName d b binderInfo =>
        have __do_jp := fun b =>
          if b.hasLooseBVars = true then pure (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key.other, todo)
          else pure (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key.arrow, (todo.push d).push b);
        if b.hasLooseBVars = true then do
          let b ← liftM (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.MatchClone.elimLooseBVarsByBeta b)
          __do_jp b
        else do
          let b ← pure b
          __do_jp b
      | x => pure (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key.other, todo)

fun {α} p entry =>
  match p with
  | (values, starIdx, children) =>
    match entry with
    | (todo, lctx, v) =>
      if todo.isEmpty = true then
        have values := values.push v;
        pure (values, starIdx, children)
      else
        have e := todo.back!;
        have todo := todo.pop;
        do
        let __x ←
          Lean.Meta.withLCtx lctx.1 lctx.2 (liftM (Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.pushArgs false todo e))
        match __x with
          | (k, todo) =>
            if (k == Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key.star) = true then
              if starIdx = 0 then do
                let starIdx ← Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.newTrie (todo, lctx, v)
                pure (values, starIdx, children)
              else do
                Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.addLazyEntryToTrie starIdx (todo, lctx, v)
                pure (values, starIdx, children)
            else
              match children[k]? with
              | none => do
                let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.newTrie (todo, lctx, v)
                have children :
                  Std.HashMap Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.Key Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.TrieIndex :=
                  children.insert k __do_lift
                pure (values, starIdx, children)
              | some idx => do
                Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.addLazyEntryToTrie idx (todo, lctx, v)
                pure (values, starIdx, children)

    have entry :=
      { stack := entry.stack, mctx := entry.mctx, labelledStars? := entry.labelledStars?,
        computedKeys := entry.computedKeys };

      (Lean.Meta.withConfig (fun x => cfg)
        (expr.withApp fun fn args =>
          have stackArgs := fun entry => do
            let entries ← Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.getStackEntries✝ fn args bvars
            pure
                { previous := entry.previous, stack := entries.reverseAux entry.stack,
                  mctx := entry.mctx, labelledStars? := entry.labelledStars?,
                  computedKeys := entry.computedKeys };
          match fn with
          | Lean.Expr.forallE n d b bi => do
            let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.mkExprInfo d bvars
            have d' : Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.StackEntry :=
              Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.StackEntry.expr __do_lift
            let b' ←

            let entry ← stackArgs entry
            let __do_lift ← Lean.getEnv
            if Lean.isClass __do_lift n = true then

                    stack := Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.StackEntry.star :: entry.stack,
                    mctx := entry.mctx, labelledStars? := entry.labelledStars?,
                    computedKeys := entry.computedKeys }

                      stack := Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.StackEntry.expr __do_lift :: entry.stack,

fun e lambdas root =>

    let __do_lift ← read
    let info ←
      liftM
          (Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.mkExprInfo e
            (lambdas ++ Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Context.bvars✝ __do_lift))
    modify fun s =>
        { previous := some info, stack := s.stack, mctx := s.mctx,
          labelledStars? := s.labelledStars?, computedKeys := s.computedKeys };
  match e.getAppFn with
  | Lean.Expr.const n us =>
    have __do_jp := fun __r =>
      have __do_jp := fun __r => pure (Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Key.const n e.getAppNumArgs);
      if (e.getAppNumArgs != 0) = true then do
        let __r ← setEAsPrevious
        __do_jp __r
      else __do_jp ();
    if root = true then __do_jp ()
    else
      match Lean.Meta.LazyDiscrTree.MatchClone.toNatLit? e with
      | some v => pure (Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Key.lit v)
      | x => __do_jp ()
  | Lean.Expr.proj n i struct => do
    setEAsPrevious
    pure (Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Key.proj n i e.getAppNumArgs)
  | Lean.Expr.fvar fvarId => do
    let __do_lift ← read
    have bvars : List Lean.FVarId := lambdas ++ Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Context.bvars✝ __do_lift
    have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.LazyM✝ Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Key :=
      fun __r =>
      match List.idxOf? fvarId bvars with
      | some idx => pure (Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Key.bvar idx e.getAppNumArgs)
      | x => pure (Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Key.fvar fvarId e.getAppNumArgs)
    if (e.getAppNumArgs != 0) = true then do
        let __r ← setEAsPrevious
        __do_jp __r

    if e.isApp = true then pure Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Key.star
    else Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.mkLabelledStar✝ mvarId

    setEAsPrevious

doc:
Evaluate the `Trie α` at index `trie`,
replacing it with the evaluated value,
and returning the `Trie α`.

Performance note: In the `apply` search discrimination tree, after root node `⟨Eq, 3⟩`,
there are about `150,000` entries in the `pending` array.
To deal with this smoothly, we parallellize the computation into chunks of `5000` entries.

def Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.evalNode✝ {α : Type} (trie : Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.TrieIndex) :
  Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.TreeM✝ α (Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Trie α)

fun {α} trie => do
  let __do_lift ← get
  have node : Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Trie α := __do_lift[trie]!
  if node.pending.isEmpty = true then pure node
    else
      have numTasks := node.pending.size / 5000 + 1;
      do
      liftM Lean.Core.checkInterrupted
      let tasks ←
        numTasks.foldM
            (fun i x tasks => do
              let __do_lift ← readThe Lean.Meta.Context
              let __do_lift_1 ← getThe Lean.Meta.State
              let __do_lift_2 ← readThe Lean.Core.Context
              let __do_lift_3 ← getThe Lean.Core.State
              let __do_lift ←
                liftM
                    (((Lean.withCurrHeartbeats
                                (Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.processPending✝ node.pending (i * 5000)
                                  ((i + 1) * 5000))).run'
                            __do_lift __do_lift_1).run'
                        __do_lift_2 __do_lift_3).asTask
              pure (tasks.push __do_lift))
            #[]
      Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.setTrie✝ trie default
      match node with
        |
        { values := values, star := star, labelledStars := labelledStars, children := children,
            pending := pending } =>
          do
          let __s ←
            forIn tasks (values, star, labelledStars, children) fun task __s =>
                have values := __s.1;
                have __s := __s.2;
                have star := __s.1;
                have __s := __s.2;
                have labelledStars := __s.1;
                have children := __s.2;
                do
                let __x ← ofExcept task.get
                match __x with
                  | (values', newEntries) =>
                    have values := values ++ values';
                    do
                    let __s ←
                      forIn newEntries (star, labelledStars, children) fun x __s =>
                          have star := __s.1;
                          have __s := __s.2;
                          have labelledStars := __s.1;
                          have children := __s.2;
                          match x with
                          | (key, entry) =>
                            match key with
                            | Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Key.labelledStar label =>
                              match labelledStars[label]? with
                              | some trie => do
                                Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.addLazyEntryToTrie✝ trie entry
                                pure (ForInStep.yield (star, labelledStars, children))
                              | x => do
                                let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.newTrie✝ entry
                                have labelledStars :
                                  Std.HashMap ℕ Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.TrieIndex :=
                                  labelledStars.insert label __do_lift
                                pure (ForInStep.yield (star, labelledStars, children))
                            | Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Key.star =>
                              match star with
                              | some trie => do
                                Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.addLazyEntryToTrie✝ trie entry
                                pure (ForInStep.yield (star, labelledStars, children))
                              | x => do
                                let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.newTrie✝ entry
                                have star : Option Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.TrieIndex :=
                                  some __do_lift
                                pure (ForInStep.yield (star, labelledStars, children))
                            | x =>
                              match children[key]? with
                              | some trie => do
                                Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.addLazyEntryToTrie✝ trie entry
                                pure (ForInStep.yield (star, labelledStars, children))
                              | x => do
                                let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.newTrie✝ entry
                                have children :
                                  Std.HashMap Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Key
                                    Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.TrieIndex :=
                                  children.insert key __do_lift
                                pure (ForInStep.yield (star, labelledStars, children))
                    have star : Option Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.TrieIndex := __s.1
                    have __s :
                      Std.HashMap ℕ Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.TrieIndex ×
                        Std.HashMap Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Key
                          Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.TrieIndex :=
                      __s.2
                    have labelledStars : Std.HashMap ℕ Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.TrieIndex := __s.1
                    have children :
                      Std.HashMap Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Key
                        Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.TrieIndex :=
                      __s.2
                    pure (ForInStep.yield (values, star, labelledStars, children))
          have values : Array α := __s.1
          have __s :
            Option Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.TrieIndex ×
              Std.HashMap ℕ Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.TrieIndex ×
                Std.HashMap Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Key Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.TrieIndex :=
            __s.2
          have star : Option Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.TrieIndex := __s.1
          have __s :
            Std.HashMap ℕ Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.TrieIndex ×
              Std.HashMap Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Key Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.TrieIndex :=
            __s.2
          have labelledStars : Std.HashMap ℕ Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.TrieIndex := __s.1
          have children :
            Std.HashMap Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Key Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.TrieIndex := __s.2

  have values : Array α := #[]

    Array (Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Key × Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.LazyEntry × α) := #[]

        have newEntries := __s.2;

doc:
Types are counted less towards the total matching score.
The reason is that types are usually implicit arguments. For example

- If the goal is `(1 : ℕ) = 1`, we could find
  - `rfl (a : α) : a = a`.
    This gets extra points for matching `1`
  - `Nat.succ.inj (n m : ℕ) (h : n.succ = m.succ) : n = m`.
    This gets extra points for matching `ℕ`

  Clearly, `rfl` is better.

- If we rewrite `|(0 : ℝ)|`, we could find
  - `abs_zero : |(0 : α)| = 0`
    This gets extra points for matching `0`
  - `Real.norm_eq_abs : ∀ (r : ℝ), ‖r‖ = |r|`
    This gets extra points for matching `ℝ`

  Clearly, `abs_zero` is better

In both examples, matching the type (`ℕ` or `ℝ`) was not very important for how good
the match actually was.

theorem Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.createImportedDiscrTree.go.eq_def✝ {α : Type} (env : Lean.Environment)
  (act :
    Lean.Name →
      Lean.ConstantInfo →
        Lean.MetaM
          (List (α × List (Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.Key × Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.LazyEntry))))
  (constantsPerTask capacityPerTask : ℕ) (cctx : Lean.Core.Context) (ngen : Lean.NameGenerator)
  (tasks : Array (Task (Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.InitResults✝ α))) (start cnt idx : ℕ) :
  Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.createImportedDiscrTree.go✝ env act constantsPerTask capacityPerTask
      cctx ngen tasks start cnt idx =
    let numModules := env.header.moduleData.size;
    if h : idx < numModules then
      have mdata := env.header.moduleData[idx];
      have cnt := cnt + mdata.constants.size;
      if cnt > constantsPerTask then
        match ngen.mkChild with
        | (childNGen, ngen) => do
          let t ←
            liftM
                (Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.createImportInitResults✝ cctx childNGen env act
                    capacityPerTask start (idx + 1)).asTask
          Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.createImportedDiscrTree.go✝ env act constantsPerTask
              capacityPerTask cctx ngen (tasks.push t) (idx + 1) 0 (idx + 1)
      else
        Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.createImportedDiscrTree.go✝ env act constantsPerTask
          capacityPerTask cctx ngen tasks start cnt (idx + 1)
    else
      if start < numModules then
        match ngen.mkChild with
        | (childNGen, snd) => do
          let t ←
            liftM
                (Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.createImportInitResults✝ cctx childNGen env act
                    capacityPerTask start numModules).asTask
          pure (tasks.push t)
      else pure tasks

fun {α} cctx env modName data mstate cstate act tree name constInfo =>
  if constInfo.isUnsafe = true then pure tree
  else
    if Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.blacklistInsertion env name = true then pure tree
    else
      have mctx :=
        { keyedConfig := { transparency := Lean.Meta.TransparencyMode.reducible }.toConfigWithKey };
      do
      let __do_lift ← (act name constInfo mctx mstate cctx cstate).toBaseIO
      match __do_lift with
        | Except.ok a =>
          pure
            (List.foldl
              (fun t x =>
                match x with
                | (val, entries) =>
                  List.foldl
                    (fun t x =>
                      match x with
                      | (key, entry) => t.push key (entry, val))
                    t entries)
              tree a)
        | Except.error e =>

fun {α} ext addEntry ty constantsPerTask capacityPerTask => do
  let ngen ← Lean.getNGen
  match ngen.mkChild with
    | (cNGen, ngen) => do
      Lean.setNGen ngen
      let __do_lift ← liftM (IO.mkRef none)
      have x : Inhabited (IO.Ref (Option (Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree α))) :=
        { default := __do_lift }
      let __do_lift ← Lean.getEnv
      have ref : IO.Ref (Option (Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree α)) := ext.getState __do_lift
      let __do_lift ← ST.Ref.get ref
      let importTree ←
        __do_lift.getDM do
            let __do_lift ← Lean.getOptions
            let __do_lift_1 ← Lean.getEnv
            Lean.profileitM Lean.Exception "RefinedDiscrTree import initialization" __do_lift
                (withTheReader Lean.Core.Context Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.withTreeCtx✝
                  (liftM
                    (Lean.Meta.RefinedDiscrTree.createImportedDiscrTree cNGen __do_lift_1 addEntry
                      constantsPerTask capacityPerTask)))
      let __x ← importTree.getMatch ty false false
      match __x with
        | (importCandidates, importTree) => do
          ST.Ref.set ref (some importTree)
          pure importCandidates

fun choice => do
  let __do_lift ← ST.Ref.get Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.rwRef
  let __do_lift_1 ← ST.Ref.get Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.grwRef
  let __do_lift_2 ← ST.Ref.get Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.appRef
  let __do_lift_3 ← ST.Ref.get Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.appAtRef
  have choice : Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.Choice :=
    { rw := choice.rw && __do_lift.isNone, grw := choice.grw && __do_lift_1.isNone,
      app := choice.app && __do_lift_2.isNone, appAt := choice.appAt && __do_lift_3.isNone }
  if Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.Choice.any✝ choice = true then do
      let __do_lift ← Lean.getEnv
      let __x ←
        Lean.Meta.foldImportedDecls { } Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.librarySearchIndexConfig✝
            (Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.Entries.addConst✝ choice __do_lift)
      match __x with
        | (tasks, errors) => do
          let pre ←
            ofExcept
                (Array.foldlM
                  (fun pre task =>
                    Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.PreDiscrTrees.append✝ pre <$> task.get)
                  { } tasks)
          have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.CoreM Unit := fun __r =>
            have __do_jp := fun __r =>
              have __do_jp := fun __r =>
                have __do_jp := fun __r => do
                  let __do_lift ← ST.Ref.get errors
                  __do_lift.forM Lean.logError;
                if choice.appAt = true then do
                  let __r ←
                    liftM
                        (Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.computeImportDiscrTrees.setIfNone✝
                          Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.appAtRef pre.appAt.toRefinedDiscrTree)
                  __do_jp __r
                else __do_jp ();
              if choice.app = true then do
                let __r ←
                  liftM
                      (Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.computeImportDiscrTrees.setIfNone✝
                        Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.appRef pre.app.toRefinedDiscrTree)
                __do_jp __r
              else __do_jp ();
            if choice.grw = true then do
              let __r ←
                liftM
                    (Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.computeImportDiscrTrees.setIfNone✝
                      Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.grwRef pre.grw.toRefinedDiscrTree)
              __do_jp __r
            else __do_jp ()
          if choice.rw = true then do
              let __r ←
                liftM
                    (Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.computeImportDiscrTrees.setIfNone✝
                      Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.rwRef pre.rw.toRefinedDiscrTree)

fun choice env entries name cinfo =>
  if cinfo.isUnsafe = true then pure entries
  else
    if Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.blacklist✝ env name = true then pure entries
    else do
      Lean.setMCtx { }
      let __x ← Lean.Meta.forallMetaTelescope cinfo.type
      match __x with
        | (xs, fst, e) =>
          match entries with
          | { rw := rw, grw := grw, app := app, appAt := appAt } =>
            have __do_jp := fun __r app =>
              have __do_jp := fun __r appAt =>
                have __do_jp := fun __r rw grw =>
                  pure { rw := rw, grw := grw, app := app, appAt := appAt };
                if (choice.rw || choice.grw) = true then
                  match e with
                  | (rel.app lhs).app rhs =>
                    match rel.getAppFn with
                    | Lean.Expr.const relName us =>
                      if
                          (match relName with
                            | `Iff => true
                            | `Eq => true
                            | x => false) =
                            true then
                        if choice.rw = true then
                          have __do_jp := fun __r rw =>
                            if
                                (!Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.isBadMatch✝ rhs &&
                                    (Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.isBadMatch✝ lhs ||
                                      !Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.isMVarSwap✝ lhs rhs)) =
                                  true then
                              do
                              let rw ←
                                Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.pushEntry✝ rw rhs
                                    { name := Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.Premise.const name,
                                      symm := true }
                              __do_jp () rw grw
                            else __do_jp () rw grw;
                          if (!Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.isBadMatch✝ lhs) = true then do
                            let rw ←
                              Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.pushEntry✝ rw lhs
                                  { name := Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.Premise.const name,
                                    symm := false }
                            __do_jp () rw
                          else __do_jp () rw
                        else __do_jp () rw grw
                      else
                        if choice.grw = true then
                          have __do_jp := fun __r grw =>
                            if (!Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.isBadMatch✝ rhs) = true then do
                              let grw ←
                                Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.pushEntry✝ grw rhs
                                    { name := Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.Premise.const name,
                                      symm := true, relName := relName }
                              __do_jp () rw grw
                            else __do_jp () rw grw;
                          if (!Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.isBadMatch✝ lhs) = true then do
                            let grw ←
                              Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.pushEntry✝ grw lhs
                                  { name := Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.Premise.const name,
                                    symm := false, relName := relName }
                            __do_jp () grw
                          else __do_jp () grw
                        else __do_jp () rw grw
                    | x => __do_jp () rw grw
                  | x => __do_jp () rw grw
                else __do_jp () rw grw;
              if choice.appAt = true then
                match xs.back? with
                | some x => do
                  let e ← Lean.Meta.inferType x
                  if (!Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.isBadMatch✝ e) = true then do
                      let appAt ←
                        Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.pushEntry✝ appAt e
                            { name := Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.Premise.const name }
                      __do_jp () appAt
                    else __do_jp () appAt
                | x => __do_jp () appAt
              else __do_jp () appAt;
            if choice.app = true then
              if (!Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.isBadMatch✝ e) = true then do
                let app ←
                  Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.pushEntry✝ app e
                      { name := Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.Premise.const name }
                __do_jp () app
              else __do_jp () app
            else __do_jp () app

fun root subExpr rwKind => do
  let __do_lift ← read
  if __do_lift.hyp?.isSome = true then pure none
    else
      if
          (match rwKind with
            | Mathlib.Tactic.ClickSuggestions.RwKind.hasBVars => true
            | x => false) =

        pure none
      else do
        let __do_lift ← read

        let __do_lift ← liftM (Lean.Meta.inferType subExpr)
        let subExpr' ← liftM (Lean.Meta.mkFreshExprMVar (some __do_lift))
        let root' ← Lean.Meta.replaceSubexpr (fun x => pure subExpr') pos root
        let e ←

                liftM __do_lift.mvarId!.applyRfl
                let __do_lift ← Lean.instantiateMVars subExpr'
                EarlyReturnT.return (some __do_lift))

doc:
Helper function to create a widget allowing to select parts of the main goal
and then display a link that will insert some tactic call.

The main argument is `mkCmdStr` which is a function creating the link text and the tactic call text.
The `helpMsg` argument is displayed when nothing is selected and `title` is used as a panel title.
The `onlyGoal` argument says whether the selected has to be in the goal. Otherwise it
can be in the local context.
The `onlyOne` argument says whether one should select only one sub-expression.
In every cases, all selected subexpressions should be in the main goal or its local context.

The last arguments `params` should not be provided so that the output
has type `Params → RequestM (RequestTask Html)` and can be fed to the `mk_rpc_widget%`
elaborator.

Note that the `pos` and `goalType` arguments to `mkCmdStr` could be extracted for the `Params`
argument but that extraction would happen in every example, hence it is factored out here.
We also make sure `mkCmdStr` is executed in the right context.

{ProofWidgets.Html.text title}
{inner}
) else pure (There is no goal to solve!)).asTask

doc:
Check whether a request has finished computing,
and return the response if so.
The request is removed from `runningRequests` the first time it is checked
and found to have finished.
Throws an error if the `rid` is invalid,
or if the request itself threw an error.

def ProofWidgets.checkRequest (rid : ProofWidgets.RequestId) :
  Lean.Server.RequestM (Lean.Server.RequestTask ProofWidgets.CheckRequestResponse)

value.text:
fun rid =>
  (do
      let __x ← ST.Ref.get ProofWidgets.runningRequests
      match __x with
        | (fst, m) =>
          match m[rid]? with
          | none =>
            throw
              (Lean.Server.RequestError.invalidParams
                (toString "Request '" ++ toString rid ++
                  toString "' has already finished, or the ID is invalid."))
          | some t => do
            let __do_lift ← liftM (IO.hasFinished t.task)
            if (!__do_lift) = true then pure ProofWidgets.CheckRequestResponse.running
              else do
                ST.Ref.modify ProofWidgets.runningRequests fun x =>
                    match x with
                    | (id, m) => (id, m.erase rid)
                match t.task.get with
                  | Except.error e => throw e
                  | Except.ok v => pure (ProofWidgets.CheckRequestResponse.done v)).asTask

doc:
The elaborator `mk_rpc_widget%` allows writing certain widgets in Lean instead of JavaScript.
Specifically, it translates an RPC method of type `MyProps → RequestM (RequestTask Html)`
into a widget component of type `Component MyProps`.

Even more specifically, we can write:
```lean
open Lean Server

structure MyProps where
  ...
  deriving RpcEncodable

@[server_rpc_method]
def MyComponent.rpc (ps : MyProps) : RequestM (RequestTask Html) :=
  ...

@[widget_module]
def MyComponent : Component MyProps :=
  mk_rpc_widget% MyComponent.rpc
```

This is convenient because we can program the logic that computes an output HTML tree
given input props in Lean directly.

⚠️ However, note that there are several limitations on what such component can do
compared to ones written natively in TypeScript or JavaScript:
- It must be pure, i.e. cannot directly store any React state.
  Child components may store state as usual.
- It cannot pass closures as props to the child components that it returns.
  For example, it is not currently possible to write click event handlers in Lean
  and pass them to a `<button onClick={..}>` child.
- Every time the input props change, the infoview has to send a message to the Lean server
  in order to invoke the RPC method.
  Thus there can be a noticeable visual delay between the input props changing
  and the display updating.
  Consequently, components whose props change at a high frequency
  (e.g. depending on the mouse position)
  should not be implemented using this method.

💡 Note that an inverse transformation is already possible.
Given `MyComponent : Component MyProps`, we can write:
```lean
open Lean Server

@[server_rpc_method]
def MyComponent.rpc (ps : MyProps) : RequestM (RequestTask Html) :=
  RequestM.asTask do
    return Html.ofComponent MyComponent ps #[]
```

fun e =>
  match e.getAppFn with
  | Lean.Expr.const declName us => do
    let __x ← Lean.getProjectionFnInfo? declName
    match __x with

                        else pure none

                    | x => pure none

fun locations goalType =>
  match locations[0]? with
  | some pos =>
    have __do_jp := fun __x =>
      match __x with
      | (expr, subexprPos, fvarUserName?) => do
        let expr ← Lean.instantiateMVars expr
        let path ← Mathlib.Tactic.Conv.Path.ofSubExprPos expr subexprPos
        let __do_lift ←
          do
            let info ← Lean.MonadRef.mkInfoFromRefPos
            let _ ← Lean.getCurrMacroScope
            let _ ← Lean.MonadQuotation.getContext
            pure
                {
                  raw :=
                    Lean.Syntax.node1 info `Lean.Parser.Tactic.Conv.skip
                      (Lean.Syntax.atom info "skip") }
        let a ← Mathlib.Tactic.Conv.pathToStx __do_lift path fvarUserName?
        pure a.raw;
    match pos with
    | { mvarId := mvarId, loc := Lean.SubExpr.GoalLocation.target subexprPos } => do
      let __x ← pure (goalType, subexprPos, none)
      __do_jp __x
    | { mvarId := mvarId, loc := Lean.SubExpr.GoalLocation.hypType fvarId subexprPos } => do
      let expr ← fvarId.getType
      let userName ← fvarId.getUserName
      let __x ← pure (expr, subexprPos, some userName)
      __do_jp __x
    | x => do
      let __x ←
        Lean.throwError
            (Lean.toMessageData
              "You must select something in the goal or in the type of a local hypothesis.")
      __do_jp __x
  | x => Lean.throwError (Lean.toMessageData "You must select something.")

doc:
Traverse an application from argument to function, accumulating arguments and consuming `pos`
(incrementing `i`) as we approach the head. If `pos[i]` tells us to enter the argument of `.app`
instead of the function at some point, we stop consuming `pos` and start counting arguments
(`some n`) until we hit the head. This gives us enough information to determine the value for
`Path.arg` once we reach the head, and then enter the argument we encountered earlier.

Note: if we instead run out of `pos` before reaching the head, the `Path` is a chain of `fun`s.

Note: `conv` does not see through `.mdata` surrounding an `.app`, so we do not here either.

doc:
The state used to handle computing non-overlapping semantic tokens. See
`handleOverlappingSemanticTokens` for a description of the problem.

Tokens are computed by iterating over every token _boundary_. At a given boundary, one of the
following things may happen:
1. We leave the range of a token, and there is no current token
2. We leave the range of a token, starting a new one
3. We start a token when there was none before

To do this, we maintain a set of tokens that could in principle occupy the interval from the last
token boundary to the one being considered. This includes tokens that are already in progress, and
potentially a new one from the input. The one with the highest priority is selected to be the next
one at each transition.

doc:
Eliminates overlapping tokens by selecting a single “best” token for each interval between token
boundaries.

While LSP allows clients to state they they can handle overlapping tokens, widely used clients such
as VS Code cannot handle them. Thus, we need to make them non-overlapping (this strictly generalizes
removal of duplicates).

Given tokens A, B, C, D as in:
```
|-----A------|  |----D----|
    |------B----------|
        |----C----|
```
with priorities C > B, B > A, B > D, we want to emit the tokens:
```
|-A-|-B-|----C----|-B-|-D--|
```
In other words, `B` is split into two regions: before and after `C`.

If two overlapping tokens have the same priority, then ties are broken as follows:
 * If the tokens start at the same position, then the shorter one is used.
 * If they have the same start position and are the same length, then the one that occurs later in
   the original input array is used.
 * If a new token starts in the middle of an existing one, and they have the same priority, then the
   new token is used.

Callers should ensure that all tokens in `tokens` designate non-empty regions of the file. In other
words, it should be true that `∀ t ∈ tokens, t.pos < t.tailPos`.

    have tokens :=

          match x_1 with
          | { pos := pos2, tailPos := tailPos2, type := type, priority := priority } =>
            decide (pos1 < pos2) || pos1 == pos2 && decide (tailPos1 ≤ tailPos2);
    have st :=
      { nonOverlapping := Array.mkEmpty (count * 11 / 10), current? := none, surrounding := [] };

                      | x => false) =

        (candidates.toList.mergeSort fun c1 c2 => decide (c1.kind.prio ≥ c2.kind.prio)).toArray

fun tree appStx =>
  match
    Lean.Elab.InfoTree.smallestInfo?
      (fun x =>
        match x with
        | Lean.Elab.Info.ofTermInfo ti =>
          ti.stx.getRangeWithTrailing? == appStx.getRangeWithTrailing?
        | x => false)
      tree with
  | some (appCtx, Lean.Elab.Info.ofTermInfo appInfo) =>
    have app := appInfo.expr;
    do
    let __x ←
      appCtx.runMetaM appInfo.lctx do
          let __do_lift ← Lean.Meta.inferType app
          let appType ← Lean.instantiateMVars __do_lift
          if (!appType.isForall) = true then pure none
            else do
              let __x ←
                Lean.PrettyPrinter.delabCore appType ∅
                    Lean.PrettyPrinter.Delaborator.delabForallWithSignature
              match __x with
                | (stx, snd) => do
                  let __do_lift ← liftM (Lean.PrettyPrinter.ppTerm { raw := stx.raw })
                  pure (some __do_lift)
    match __x with
      | some fmt =>
        pure (some { signatures := #[{ label := toString fmt }], activeSignature? := some 0 })
      | x => pure none
  | x => pure none

doc:
Finds all `CompletionInfo`s (both from the `InfoTree` and synthetic ones), prioritizes them,
arranges them in partitions of `CompletionInfo`s with the same priority and sorts these partitions
so that `CompletionInfo`s with the highest priority come first.
The returned `CompletionInfo`s are also tagged with their index in `findCompletionInfosAt` so that
when resolving a `CompletionItem`, we can reconstruct which `CompletionInfo` it was created from.

In general, the `InfoTree` may contain multiple different `CompletionInfo`s covering `hoverPos`,
and so we need to decide which of these `CompletionInfo`s we want to use to show completions to the
user. We choose priorities by the following rules:
- Synthetic completions have the lowest priority since they are only intended as a backup.
- Non-identifier completions have the highest priority since they tend to be much more helpful than
  identifier completions when available since there are typically way too many of the latter.
- Within the three groups [non-id completions, id completions, synthetic completions],
  `CompletionInfo`s with a smaller range are considered to be better.

  | (infos, isComplete) =>
    have partitions := Lean.Server.Completion.computePrioritizedCompletionPartitions✝ infos.zipIdx;
    (partitions, isComplete)

doc:
Generate completion items for a syntax object generated by `identWithPartialTrailingDot` given a
known collection of completion candidates. Should only be used in contexts where namespaces do not
affect the set of eligible completion candidates.

signature.text:
def Lean.Server.Completion.trailingDotCompletion✝.{u_1, u_2} {Coll : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2}
  [ForIn Id Coll (Lean.Name × α)] (entries : Coll) (stx : Lean.Syntax)
  (caps : Lean.Lsp.ClientCapabilities) (ctx : Lean.Elab.ContextInfo)
  (mkItem : Lean.Name → α → Option Lean.Lsp.InsertReplaceEdit → Lean.Lsp.ResolvableCompletionItem) :
  Array Lean.Lsp.ResolvableCompletionItem

value.text:
fun {Coll} {α} [ForIn Id Coll (Lean.Name × α)] entries stx caps ctx mkItem =>
  (match
      match stx.getSubstring? false false with
      | none => ("", false)
      | some ss =>
        if
            (!String.Pos.Raw.atEnd ss.str ss.stopPos &&
                String.Pos.Raw.get ss.str ss.stopPos == '.') =
              true then
          (ss.toString ++ ".", true)
        else (ss.toString, false) with
    | (partialName, trailingDot) =>
      have items := #[];
      do
      let __s ←
        forIn entries items fun x __s =>
            have items := __s;
            match x with
            | (name, value) =>
              if partialName.charactersIn name.toString = true then
                have textEdit? :=
                  if
                      (!Option.any
                            (fun x =>
                              Option.any
                                (fun x =>
                                  Option.any
                                    (fun x => Option.any (fun x => x) x.insertReplaceSupport?)
                                    x.completionItem?)
                                x.completion?)
                            caps.textDocument?) =
                        true then
                    none
                  else
                    match stx.getRange? with
                    | some { start := start, stop := stop } =>
                      have stop := if trailingDot = true then stop + ' ' else stop;
                      have range :=
                        { start := ctx.fileMap.utf8PosToLspPos start,
                          «end» := ctx.fileMap.utf8PosToLspPos stop };
                      some { newText := name.toString, insert := range, replace := range }
                    | x => none;
                have items := items.push (mkItem name value textEdit?);
                pure (ForInStep.yield items)
              else pure (ForInStep.yield items)
      have items : Array Lean.Lsp.ResolvableCompletionItem := __s
      pure items).run

fun {m} [Monad m] [Lean.MonadEnv m] [MonadLiftT Lean.MetaM m] [Lean.Server.MonadCancellable m] f =>
  do
  let _ ←
    (Lean.Server.Completion.forEligibleDeclsM fun decl ci => do
            modify fun x => x + 1
            let __do_lift ← get
            have __do_jp : Unit → StateT ℕ m PUnit.{1} := fun __r => liftM (f decl ci)
            if __do_lift ≥ 10000 then do
                Lean.Server.RequestCancellation.check
                let __r ← set 0
                __do_jp __r
              else __do_jp ()).run
        0
  pure ()

fun uri pos completionInfoPos ctx stx caps =>
